MSCI.thesis_one_line: Runs the benchmark indexes trillions of dollars track and raised cash-flow guidance on real growth, but on corrected inputs (SBC-burdened, unlevered, 5.17% risk-free rate) the price needs about 10% growth for ten years against a 9% base, so it is a watch-list name until the price or the guide moves.
kill_criteria: Organic recurring subscription Run Rate growth falls below 6% for two consecutive quarters (currently 8.1%, Q2 2026).

Company-wide Retention Rate falls below 92% for two consecutive quarters (currently 95.3%, Q2 2026; 94.4% a year ago in Q2 2025 -- the metric itself has some seasonal/measurement noise, so two-quarter persistence is the trigger).
Asset-based fee Run Rate growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters (a direct read on AUM-linked revenue sensitivity to a market downturn).
FY guidance is cut (as opposed to raised/reaffirmed) at any subsequent quarterly release -- track record is currently initiate -> reaffirm -> raise.
Upgrade trigger (not a kill): price at or below about $470, or an FY27 free-cash-flow guide midpoint of at least $1.70bn (about +12%) (added 6 Oct 2026).

Governance check: no permanent Chief Accounting Officer named, or any material weakness or restatement, by the FY2026 10-K (Feb 2027); the CFO is interim principal accounting officer since 10 Aug 2026 (added 6 Oct 2026).
key_adverse_facts: Q4 2025 GAAP diluted EPS fell 2.3% YoY (to $3.81) even as Adjusted EPS rose 11.5% (to $4.66) -- driven by higher interest expense on higher debt and an $11.8m write-off of a minority investee.

Q1 2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $5.53 includes an $88m one-off tax benefit from an internal legal-entity restructuring, explicitly excluded from adjusted guidance metrics -- the headline GAAP number overstates underlying run-rate earnings growth.
Weighted-average diluted share count down 5.9% YoY on buybacks that are partly debt-funded; total debt has risen even as buybacks continue.
Guidance is conditioned on the First Street acquisition closing in Q3 2026, which remains subject to regulatory approval -- a real, if small (~$120m cash), closing-condition risk.

Asset-based fees are 27.3% of Run Rate but supplied 51% of the past year's Run Rate growth (asset-based +25.2% vs subscriptions +7.8%); the 10-11% base extrapolated a market-linked growth rate (Q2 2026 release).

Guided FCF ($1,485-1,545m) adds back about $129m of stock-based compensation and is after about $284m of interest; the original DCF divided it into enterprise value at a 9.0% rate. Corrected, implied growth is about 10.1% versus a 9% base (6 Oct 2026).
Global Controller and Chief Accounting Officer resigned 27 Mar 2026; since 10 Aug 2026 the CFO is interim principal accounting officer (8-Ks 31 Mar and 7 Aug 2026).
data_conflicts: The b1 quant composite ranks MSCI only mid-pack (live_rank 250/~2,300, decile 5) despite the triage's 'quality 5, growth 4' framing -- the gap is explained by weak value-family percentiles (pct_ebit_ev 5th, pct_bp 35th), i.e. the model correctly flags MSCI as expensive on classic value ratios even though the business quality is real.
MSCI.confidence_in_thesis: medium -- business facts (Run Rate +12.0%, retention 95.3%, guidance raised) are primary-sourced, but the valuation premise was an artefact of an SBC add-back, a levered-FCF-over-EV mismatch and a stale rate; at the corrected inputs the price exceeds value at the 9% base case

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: Re-assessed 6 Oct 2026 (RA6). EV $46.15bn (market cap $40.08bn + principal debt $6.425bn - cash $0.356bn). Unlevered, SBC-burdened FY26 FCF $1,616m (guided FCF $1,515m - SBC about $129m + after-tax interest about $230m); WACC 9.5% (rf 5.17% + Blume beta 1.147 x ERP 4.5% = Ke 10.3%; after-tax Kd 4.5%; 9.2% to 10.0% across ERP 4.14-5.0%); terminal 3.5%: implied 10-yr FCF CAGR 10.1% (9.4% to 11.3%), equity cross-check 8.6% to 10.3%. Base 9% (subscriptions +8% on 73% of Run Rate, asset-based fees normalised to about 10%). Value at base $500 (-9%; -18% to -3%). The original 9.7% reproduces only on a 9.0% rate with levered, SBC-inflated FCF over EV.
valuation_view_vs_v1.note: Corrected from 'below' to above: stale rate, SBC add-back, levered-FCF-over-EV mismatch, and a base case that extrapolated market-linked fee growth.

MSCI.scenario_basis: Starting NTM adjusted EPS ~$21.77 (d4 snapshot), price $551.36; bear/base/bull EPS growth 4%/11%/16%; exit P/E restated 18x/22.5x/26x (was 20x/25x/27x; the corrected base value is 23x NTM EPS); dividend $8.20 growing with EPS. Original arithmetic (-2.2%/+12.0%/+19.9%) re-checked and correct; only the exit multiples changed.

NEE.thesis_one_line: America's biggest utility plus its biggest wind-and-solar builder, guiding 8%-plus earnings growth for a decade at a price implying almost none of it.
kill_criteria: Full-year adjusted EPS comes in below the low end of the then-current guidance range (currently $3.92) at any year-end report.
Consolidated debt/(debt+equity) rises above ~68% (from ~63.4% today) without a credible deleveraging plan, or NEE/NEECH/FPL suffers a credit-rating downgrade.
FPL's next base rate proceeding (post the 2025 four-year settlement expires ~2029) is resolved with an allowed ROE or capital-recovery mechanism materially worse than the current settlement.
The 2023 securities class action settlement ($150m, insurance-covered) or the XPLR securities/derivative litigation is not given final court approval and reopens as active, uninsured exposure.

NEER backlog-to-in-service conversion stalls (two consecutive quarters of GW placed into service below the trailing-four-quarter average), signalling supply-chain, interconnection or financing bottlenecks.
key_adverse_facts: Pending combination with Dominion Energy (agreement dated 15 May 2026; 0.8138 NEE shares plus a $360m aggregate cash amount per Dominion share; NEE holders approved 3 Sep 2026 incl. authorised-share increase from 3.2bn to 5.0bn; state, FERC and NRC approvals pending, close expected 2H 2027; reciprocal break fees $2.24bn / $6.52bn / $4.83bn) was omitted from the original dossier; stand-alone share count, leverage and growth figures will not hold post-close (DV30).

2023 political-activity securities class action settled for $150m (insurance-covered), pending final court approval; related shareholder derivative actions settled for insurers to pay NEE ~$16m, also pending court approval.

XPLR Energy (former NextEra Energy Partners) securities class action (filed July 2025, amended Jan 2026) and a related unitholder derivative action name NEE and NEE-affiliated executives; motion to dismiss pending as of March 2026.
Avangrid v. NextEra Energy antitrust suit (originally sought $350m, trebled) -- federal/state antitrust claims dismissed Sept 2025, remaining Massachusetts state-law claims pending.

Consolidated long-term debt (non-current) rose 10.3% in six months ($89.6bn to $98.8bn) funding the FPL and NEER capital plans; the DV30 dividend-basis DCF shows the price already requires about 8%/yr dividend growth, so the stock is fairly priced for the guide, not cheap.
data_conflicts: Triage's red flag cited only Florida hurricane/wildfire physical risk; this dossier's primary-source work found additional, more financially material items (XPLR/Avangrid/political-activity litigation, fast-rising consolidated debt) that the triage pass did not surface.
NEE.confidence_in_thesis: low-medium -- primary-sourced guidance and segment data are clean, but the stand-alone thesis predates a transformational pending merger and the corrected valuation is in line with, not far below, the growth guide (DV30)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for NEE. Verification DV30 (2026-10-08) re-ran the valuation on a dividend basis (utility FCF is negative; the original treated EPS as cash flow and used a 4.2% risk-free rate): D0 $2.49 (4 x $0.6232), cost of equity 7.82% (5.17% + 0.64 x 4.14%), terminal growth 2.5-3.0%, price $76.08: the price needs 7.5-8.4%/yr dividend growth for ten years versus management's 8%+ EPS growth guide (dividend guide 6%/yr 2027-2028), so implied_vs_base is in_line, not 'below by a wide margin'. The original ~1.2% implied EPS CAGR was an artefact of EPS-as-cash and a 7.0% rate. The valuation is also stand-alone: it ignores the pending all-stock-plus-$360m-cash combination with Dominion Energy (0.8138 NEE shares per Dominion share, announced 18 May 2026, NEE shareholders approved 3 Sep 2026, close expected 2H 2027, $6.52bn reciprocal break fee).

NEE.scenario_basis: Starting FY2026 guided adjusted EPS midpoint $3.97, price $76.08; bear/base/bull EPS growth 3%/8%/11%; exit P/E 15x/18x/20x; dividend yield ~3.27% growing with EPS.

ORLY.thesis_one_line: Auto-parts retailer with 33 straight years of sales growth and two guidance raises in 2026, but the price already discounts more total free-cash-flow growth than the evidence supports.
kill_criteria: Comparable store sales growth falls below 2% for two consecutive quarters (from +6.0% currently).
Gross margin falls below 51.0% of sales for two consecutive quarters (currently 51.5-51.8%).
Lease-adjusted debt/EBITDAR (company-defined; 2.17x at 30-Jun-2026) rises above 2.5x without an offsetting reason (e.g. large M&A).
SG&A growth outpaces sales growth for three consecutive quarters (as already flagged once by management in Q4 2025 -- 'SG&A expenses again exceeded our expectations').
Net new store openings miss the guided 225-235 range for FY2026.
key_adverse_facts: Management has twice acknowledged SG&A running hotter than its own expectations (health care and casualty-claim cost inflation), most recently in the Q4 2025 release.

Shareholders' deficit of $1.84bn (30 Jun 2026) -- a deliberate feature of the aggressive buyback model, not distress, but it means there is no equity cushion beyond the business's own cash generation in a downside scenario.

Long-term debt (including commercial paper) rose 16.6% in six months (Dec 2025 to Jun 2026), specifically to help fund buybacks -- leverage is moderate (net debt/EBITDA ~1.4-1.5x excluding leases; the company's lease-adjusted adjusted debt/EBITDAR was 2.17x at 30-Jun-2026 against a 2.5x kill threshold) and the trend is up.
data_conflicts: Triage's 'quality 5, growth 4' framing is not fully corroborated by the b1 quant composite, which ranks ORLY only in the third decile (live_rank 363/~2,300), driven mainly by weak 12-1 month momentum (23rd percentile) and expensive value percentiles -- a timing/momentum tension, not a fundamentals conflict; this dossier resolves it in favor of the fundamentals given the accelerating comp-sales trend and clean guidance-raise record.
ORLY.confidence_in_thesis: high -- operating results, the guidance track record and the balance sheet are all directly primary-sourced and internally consistent; the only real uncertainty is whether the price already reflects the good news

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for ORLY. The dossier's reverse DCF (EV ~$76.4bn, FCF $1.95bn, 8.5%, 3.5% terminal) reproduces at 11.6% but compared total-FCF growth with a base that includes 3-4 points of per-share buyback uplift. Like-for-like the total-FCF base is ~7-8%; restated on the programme basis (equity basis, market cap $69.66bn, FCF after SBC $1,914M, Ke 8.1% to 9.3%, ten years then 3%) the implied 10-year FCF growth is 10.4% to 13.6%, i.e. above the base. implied_vs_base moves from in_line to above and the verdict from INCLUDE-SMALL to WATCH (programme precedent: DIS, DLR).

ORLY.scenario_basis: Starting FY2026 guided diluted EPS midpoint $3.25, price $86.115; bear/base/bull EPS growth 4%/11%/15%; exit P/E 20x/24x/26x; no dividend.
